title: Breaking Down the Israel–Iran Conflict: What We Know So Far - Day 10
byline: This guide answers the most important questions about the Israel Iran war that is unfolding right now. The United States and Israel have launched major military strikes on Iran and Iran has responded with missile attacks across the region. This is one of the most serious escalations in the Middle East in years.

title: How is Sri Lanka responding to the Israel–Iran conflict: Day 10
byline: As tensions escalate between Israel and Iran, Sri Lanka has taken a series of diplomatic, aviation and precautionary measures to manage potential fallout and safeguard its citizens. Here is how Sri Lanka is responding.

title: G7 to take ’necessary measures’ to support energy supplies
byline: G7 nations have said they are ready to take ’’necessary measures’’ to support the global supply of energy after the US-Israel war with Iran sent oil prices surging.

title: IRIS Dena attack: Iranian sailors died due to multiple injuries, drowning
byline: The head of the team of Judicial Medical Officers who performed the postmortem on the bodies of Iranian navy personnel, Prof. U.C.P.Perera said the death had occurred to them due to multiple injuries and drowning

title: Low number of Israeli tourists in Arugam Bay amid off-season and regional tensions
byline: The number of Israeli tourists currently staying in Arugam Bay remains low due to the off-season, although security measures in the area continue to remain tight, a senior police officer said.

title: National carrier takes new route via Afghanistan, Azerbaijan for European destinations
byline: Following the closure of Middle Eastern airspace, SriLankan Airlines, the national carrier, has adopted an alternative route through Afghanistan and Azerbaijan for its European destinations, an official said.

title: Viking Sky cruise ship calls in Colombo with 700 tourists
byline: The luxury cruise liner Viking Sky called at the Port of Colombo yesterday, bringing around 700 international travellers to Sri Lanka, as part of its voyage from Thailand to the Maldives, adding fresh momentum to the island’s cruise tourism segment.

title: Samsung Sri Lanka opens  pre-orders for Galaxy S26 series
byline: Samsung Sri Lanka has officially opened pre-orders for the highly anticipated Galaxy S26 Series, introducing its most advanced AI-powered smartphones yet to customers across the island.

title: Regulatory void leaves virtual asset sector exposed to financial crimes
byline: Sri Lanka’s financial landscape is facing new challenges, as an unregulated virtual asset market opens potential avenues for financial crimes.

title: Week begins on a negative note
byline: Indices closed in red as a result of price losses in counters such as Commercial Bank, Hatton National Bank and John Keells Holdings with the turnover crossing Rs. 5.8 Bn.

title: Litro gas prices increased
byline: Litro Gas Lanka has announced a revision of domestic gas cylinder prices with effect from midnight on March 10, 2026, citing rising gas prices in the global market.

title: Trump says he doesn’t believe Iran’s new supreme leader ’can live in peace’
byline: US President Donald Trump said he doubts Iran’s newly appointed Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei can coexist peacefully with Washington, reiterating his dissatisfaction with Tehran’s choice of leadership.

title: Energy Minister agrees to key union demands, Presidential talks on salary hike within two days
byline: The Energy Minister has agreed to several proposals submitted by electricity trade unions during a discussion held today (10) with the boards of four newly established power sector companies following the restructuring of the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB).

title: Iran says bodies of sailors killed near Sri Lanka to be repatriated
byline: Iran has announced that the bodies of dozens of sailors who were killed when the vessel IRIS Dena was attacked and sunk near Sri Lanka will soon be returned to the country.

title: CSE Rebounds Strongly as Improved Oil Supply Outlook Lifts Investor Sentiment
byline: The Colombo market staged a strong recovery on 10th March 2026, regaining positive momentum following encouraging developments surrounding global oil supply and signs of easing tensions in the Middle East. The improved external outlook provided a positive breather for the CSE after the recent sharp correction, with both indices closing significantly higher as the majority of counters ended the session in green territory.

title: Over 600 kg of narcotics found in seized fishing vessel
byline: Over 600 kilograms of narcotics have been discovered in a multi-day fishing vessel seized by the Sri Lanka Navy on suspicion of transporting a large consignment of drugs, Minister of Public Security and Parliamentary Affairs Ananda Wijepala said.

title: SC continues hearing of carrom board case appeals
byline: The hearings into the appeal applications filed by former Sports Minister Mahindananda Aluthgamage and former Lanka Sathosa Chairman Nalin Fernando, challenging the legality of the High Court judgment that convicted and sentenced them in connection with the controversial carrom board case, were taken up before the Supreme Court of Sri Lanka today for the second consecutive day.

title: US says Tuesday ‘will be our most intense day of strikes’
byline: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said that Tuesday would be the most intense day of strikes against Iran in the campaign so far.

title: 541 drivers and conductors recruited as SLTB reorganisation begins
byline: The government has initiated the reorganisation of the Sri Lanka Transport Board (SLTB) under a national programme aimed at maintaining the country’s public transport service in a more efficient and systematic manner.

title: Gains for Sri Lanka and New Zealand  stars on rankings update
byline: Several New Zealand players have made gains in the latest rankings update, while Sri Lanka’s stars have climbed the T20I charts less than three months before the start of the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup.

title: Limit travel and fuel purchases, CPC chairman tells public
byline: Chairman of the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC), D.J. Rajakaruna has urged the public to reduce non-essential travel and use fuel sparingly in view of the energy challenges arising from the ongoing conflicts in the Middle East.

title: Putin, Trump hold phone call, discuss Iran and Ukraine wars
byline: U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin discussed the war in Iran and ‌prospects for peace in Ukraine on Monday, hours after the Kremlin chief warned that a global energy crisis threatened the world economy.

title: SC grants leave to proceed in FR petition over Royal College grade one admission
byline: The Supreme Court has granted leave to proceed with a Fundamental Rights petition filed in relation to the admission of a child to Grade One at Royal College, Colombo, after determining that there were sufficient grounds to examine an alleged violation of the right to equality guaranteed under Article 12(1) of the Constitution.

title: Namal questions fuel price hike despite 45-day oil reserve claim
byline: Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa has raised concerns over the recent increase in fuel prices, saying it contradicts government assurances that the country has oil reserves sufficient for 45 days.

title: Madagascar military leader dissolves government in surprise move
byline: Madagascar’s military ruler Col Michael Randrianirina has dissolved the government unexpectedly, dismissing the prime minister and the entire cabinet, according to a statement from his spokesperson.

title: Electricity trade unions continue strike
byline: Twenty-five electricity trade unions have decided to continue their industrial action as they did not receive any favourable response from the six new state-owned companies formed following the dissolution of the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB).

title: Former CID DIG Prasad Ranasinghe arrested over corruption allegations
byline: Former Deputy Inspector General of Police of the Criminal Investigation Department, Prasad Ranasinghe, was arrested by officers of the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption on corruption charges.

title: Sri Lanka grants fee visa extensions for foreigners affected by Middle East flight cancellations
byline: The Sri Lanka government has approved visa extensions on a fee basis for foreign nationals unable to leave the country due to flight cancellations to the Middle East, caused by the ongoing military situation in the region.

title: Committee forms to monitor economic impact of Middle East crisis
byline: In response to the ongoing war in the Middle East and its potential impact on the economy, the Sri Lanka government has established an Economic Monitoring Committee to track and address emerging economic challenges.

title: Sri Lanka Coast Guard, Navy seize 6.8 kg of gold, arrest two suspects
byline: Based on naval intelligence, a joint operation by the Sri Lanka Coast Guard and the Sri Lanka Navy off the waters of Kankesanthurai led to the arrest of two suspects.

title: 475 killed in road accidents so far in 2026
byline: A total of 457 fatal road accidents have been reported across Sri Lanka so far in 2026, resulting in 475 deaths, DIG in-charge of Traffic Control and Road Safety W. P. J. Senadheera said.

title: Cabinet approves visa exemption agreement between Sri Lanka and Nepal
byline: The Cabinet Ministers has approved a proposal to sign an agreement between Sri Lanka and Nepal to exempt holders of diplomatic, official and service passports from obtaining visas.

title: Fuel price hike aimed at preventing bigger increase later: PSTC
byline: The recent fuel price increase in Sri Lanka was implemented to avoid a much larger hike in the coming weeks as global oil prices are expected to rise, a senior official said.

title: BCCI announce Rs 131 crore cash reward for Team India after T20 World Cup 2026 win
byline: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) on Tuesday announced a whopping Rs. 131 crore prize money for the senior men’s Indian side that clinched the T20 World Cup 2026 title over New Zealand in Ahmedabad on Sunday.

title: Govt signs Rs. 3bn number plate printing agreement
byline: The official agreement to transfer the printing of vehicle number plates in the country to a new private company under a Rs. 3 billion project was signed today.

title: World must push for peace: Sajith
byline: The world must push for peace and get the parties involved in the conflict in the Middle East to the negotiating table, Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa said today.

title: Pakistan to close schools, take other measures to cut energy as oil spikes
byline: Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ‌said on Monday that schools would close for two weeks and office workers would work more from home as he announced a range of measures to cut fuel use and government spending to cope ​with surging oil prices due to the Iran war.

title: Australia grants asylum to five Iranian women footballers
byline: Australia has agreed to provide visas to five members of the Iranian women’s football team, allowing them to stay in the country, as they could face punishment upon their return home for not singing the Iranian national anthem before their first match at an Asian Cup tournament.

title: Two men charged with using weapon of mass destruction near New York City mayor’s home
byline: Two men face charges of providing material support to a terrorist organization and using a weapon of mass destruction after a pair of homemade bombs were tossed during protests near New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s home Saturday, court documents show.

title: Opposition to bring in no faith motion against Energy Minister: Marikkar
byline: The Opposition is to bring in a no faith motion against Minister of Power and Energy Kumara Jayakody next week, MP S.M. Marikkar told a media briefing today.
